idiom_name: enum Step with an associated closure value and a while-case driver
implementation_notes: Swift makes no guarantee about tail calls, so mutual recursion that must survive unbounded depth is written by hand: a Step enum with an associated value for the finished case and an associated closure for the suspended case, driven by a while loop that matches the cases. Closures are first-class values of function type and are reference types when they capture, so the step must capture its parameters by value (the default for a closure over locals in a function argument position) and must not rely on the producing frame staying alive. Use it for parsers and tree walks with data-driven depth; a bounded recursion is clearer and faster as a plain function.
pitfalls: A step closure that captures self or a class instance keeps it alive for as long as the chain runs; capture lists are the tool for breaking the retain cycle the chain would otherwise create.
Each step allocates a closure and a boxed enum payload, and ARC adds retain/release traffic on top - a plain loop over an array state is dramatically cheaper where it applies.
A runaway recursion now exhausts memory instead of crashing with a stack overflow, so the failure is slower and harder to attribute unless the driver counts steps.
